chunks: God advances the example of a man who is owned (as slave in common) by a number of men at loggerheads, and another man who is owned by only one. Are these two alike in attribute? God be praised; yet many of them do not know.

key_terms.بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ: Yet most of them do not know

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the metaphor of the shared slave versus the devoted slave in Surah Az-Zumar?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse (39:29) is often interpreted through the lens of *Tawhid* (monotheism) versus *Shirk* (polytheism), where the 'quarrelsome masters' symbolize the conflicting attributes or deities worshipped by polytheists, leading to internal discord. The 'slave at peace' represents the believer whose heart is unified in submission to Allah, illustrating that spiritual coherence yields greater stability than the fragmented devotion of the polytheist. This metaphor underscores the practical implication that true worship requires undivided loyalty, a concept central to Imam Ali’s teachings on the purity of faith.
